definitions.explanation: Money given to the bereaved family at funerals or memorial services. Presented in special envelopes with appropriate formatting.
A euphemism for death, funerals, or other unfortunate events.

examples.japanese: {不祝儀|ぶしゅうぎ}{袋|ぶくろ}に{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I wrote my name on the condolence money envelope.

examples.japanese: {不祝儀|ぶしゅうぎ}の{相場|そうば}は{関係性|かんけいせい}によって{異|こと}なる。
examples.english: The appropriate amount for condolence money varies depending on the relationship.

examples.japanese: {不祝儀|ぶしゅうぎ}があって{急|きゅう}に{帰省|きせい}することになった。
examples.english: A death in the family came up, so I have to suddenly return home.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: {不|ふ} (un-, non-) + {祝儀|しゅうぎ} (congratulatory gift). Literally "non-celebratory gift," a euphemism for funeral money.

CONTRAST WITH {祝儀|しゅうぎ}:
・{祝儀|しゅうぎ}: money given at happy events (weddings, births)
・{不祝儀|ぶしゅうぎ}: money given at sad events (funerals, memorials)

ENVELOPE ETIQUETTE:
・Use {不祝儀|ぶしゅうぎ}{袋|ぶくろ} (special mourning envelopes)
・Black and white or silver ties on envelope
・Write name in {薄墨|うすずみ} (light ink) traditionally
・Never use new bills (fold them once first)

APPROPRIATE AMOUNTS (general guide):
・{知人|ちじん} (acquaintance): 3,000-5,000{円|えん}
・{友人|ゆうじん} (friend): 5,000-10,000{円|えん}
・{親戚|しんせき} (relative): 10,000-50,000{円|えん}
・{親|おや} (parent): 50,000-100,000{円|えん}

RELATED TERMS:
・{香典|こうでん} (incense money - synonym for funeral offering)
・{御霊前|ごれいぜん} (offering to the spirit)
・{御仏前|ごぶつぜん} (offering to the Buddha)
・{弔問|ちょうもん} (condolence visit)
